**5B.7 Research Note: Evidence vs. Slogans / Patronage / Scapegoating**
**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning positive on policy design and diagnosis, but with clear pockets of patronage, threat-framing, and weak openness to scrutiny.

**Accepted claims**
- **IMF Executive Board Concludes Post Financing Assessment with Nigeria** | IMF | 2024-02-09 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa  
  The IMF said Tinubu moved ahead with subsidy removal and FX unification, created a fiscal/tax reform committee, and paired austerity with cereals, subsidized fertilizer, wage awards, and diesel VAT suspension to soften the shock. This is strong evidence of policy based on diagnosis and partial correction rather than slogan-only politics.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Tinubu Establishes Comprehensive Economic Coordination and Planning System for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/  
  Tinubu created PECC/EET structures centered on the finance minister and CBN governor, with economists and major private-sector figures, and ordered rapid implementation of an emergency economic plan. That is direct evidence of technocratic, evidence-aware coordination.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Tinubu Directs Reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/  
  Procurement reform is a concrete corrective move aimed at transparency and value for money. It is one of the clearest anti-slippage signals in the record.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`

- **Tinubu Appoints New Director General of the Bureau of Public Enterprises** | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-director-general-of-the-bureau-of-public-enterprises/  
  The appointment was framed around a financial expert and chartered accountant advancing fiduciary discipline and private-sector-driven reform. That supports a technocratic, evidence-based staffing pattern in a key economic institution.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`

- **World Bank: Turning the Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms  
  The Bank said the reform package reduced distortions and improved transparency, especially by eliminating the official/parallel FX gap and phasing out the regressive fuel subsidy. It also said the changes were painful in the short run, which is consistent with evidence-based correction under real-world constraints.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **World Bank: Supporting Nigeria Homegrown Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification  
  The World Bank said the reform package was aimed at raising non-oil revenue, safeguarding oil revenue, and creating fiscal space for public services, while supporting vulnerable households. This is strong external validation of a policy program grounded in diagnosis rather than slogans.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Tinubu Directs Prioritization of Digital Infrastructure Investment to Enhance Business Efficiency and Productivity** | State House | 2024-03-14 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-prioritization-of-digital-infrastructure-investment-to-enhance-business-efficiency-and-productivity/  
  Tinubu ordered ministries to align regulations and tax frameworks to accelerate broadband and telecom investment. That is a specific regulatory correction, not mere rhetoric.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.6`

- **Nigeria and U.S. Reach Agreement to Harness Artificial Intelligence, Facilitate Data Flows, and Empower Digital Upskilling** | Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy | 2024-07-27 | https://fmcide.gov.ng/u-s-nigeria-reach-agreement-to-harness-artificial-intelligence-facilitate-data-flows-and-empower-digital-upskilling-issue-joint-statement/  
  Nigeria publicly committed to open, interoperable, secure internet language plus AI cooperation and workforce upskilling. This is evidence of policy that engages expert inputs and capacity-building rather than empty slogans.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.6`

- **Tinubu Calls for Suspension of Sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso** | State House | 2024-02-24 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/  
  Tinubu urged ECOWAS to choose “a better path” through negotiation and improved governance. This is not economic policy per se, but it is a direct counterexample to reflexive scapegoating and punitive escalation.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.4`

**Counterevidence**
- **Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency** | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/  
  The appointment of Tinubu’s son-in-law to the Federal Housing Authority is the clearest nepotism signal in the 2024 record. It directly weakens the claim that economic governance was insulated from patronage.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **President Tinubu I Have No Cabal or Sponsors To Compensate** | State House | 2024-07-26 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/  
  Tinubu publicly denied owing a cabal or sponsors. This is relevant as a rebuttal to patronage claims, but it is rhetoric, not proof, and it sits uneasily beside the son-in-law appointment.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **Nigeria Has Detained Journalist Who Reported on Corruption in Widening Crackdown** | Reuters via GPB | 2024-05-09 | https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown  
  Detaining a journalist over corruption reporting suggests an environment where scrutiny of elites is punished. That undercuts evidence-based correction because it discourages bad-news reporting.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **4 Nigerian Journalists Charged With Cybercrime/Defamation Over Fraud Investigation** | CPJ | 2024-02-09 | https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/  
  Criminal charges for reporting on corruption are negative evidence for policy grounded in open evidence gathering.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **Nigeria Police Charge 4 Journalists With Cybercrimes for Corruption Reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/  
  The continued use of cybercrime law against journalists shows that the information environment remained punitive. That is a bad sign for correction and accountability.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **Nigeria Considers Tough Penalties for ‘Subversive’ Acts Under Proposed Law** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-14 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782  
  A proposed counter-subversion bill was criticized as a crackdown on dissent. Even though later withdrawn, it points toward scapegoating and a chilled policy climate rather than open correction.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.5`

- **Hundreds Gather Across Nigerian Cities to Protest Cost-of-Living Crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376  
  Reuters linked protests to subsidy removal, naira devaluation, electricity tariffs, and inflation above 34 percent. This shows the reform path generated real pain and that policy success was not yet validated by outcomes.  
  IDs: `5B.7`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence of technocratic reform, external validation, and some corrective policy moves.
- I found weaker direct evidence of explicit course-correction after policy failure beyond palliatives, procurement reform, and institutional reorganization.
- I did not find clear public examples in 2024 of Tinubu personally admitting a major economic-policy mistake and reversing course because of it. The negative side is therefore strongest on patronage, repression of scrutiny, and scapegoating-by-frame, not on outright denial of all problems.
